name: Bab Al Shams, A Rare Finds Desert Resort
positioning: Fort-style desert resort on the edge of Dubai's Al Marmoom Desert Conservation Reserve, reimagined as the first hotel in Kerzner's Rare Finds portfolio
best_for: Families who want desert activities and villas that fit up to four adults
Couples who want a private pool villa looking onto the dunes

facts.text: Bab Al Shams is a low-slung desert resort modeled after an Arabian fort.
The reimagined Bab Al Shams is the first property in Kerzner's Rare Finds portfolio of destination-focused hotels.
The resort sits on the edge of the Al Marmoom Desert Conservation Reserve.
Rooms are spread over adobe-walled blocks among palms and native ghaf trees, linked by winding paths with water features.
The resort offers one- and two-bedroom Desert Pool Villas.
The Two-Bedroom Villa suits families or groups of up to four adults.
Three large swimming pools look out over the desert.
The spa offers speciality facials, massages and traditional hammam experiences.
A sound bath experience takes place in the spa's outdoor desert area.
Al Hadheerah is an open-air dinner spectacular serving Middle Eastern cuisine with live performances.
Anwa is a rooftop lounge with sunsets, cocktails and Pan-Asian dishes.
Family activities include an adventure playground with a kid-sized zipline, guided nature walks, camel and pony rides, falconry, and Arabic calligraphy and coffee-making sessions.

highlights.text: Each Desert Pool Villa has a private pool, views of golden dunes and a dedicated Villa Host.
Guided 4x4 desert drives cross the Al Marmoom Desert Conservation Reserve, where guests might spot the Arabian oryx.
Private hot-air balloon rides take in the Margam desert from above.
Camelback trekking is offered and is accessible for all ages.
The resort has rental bikes and guided electric fat-bike tours through the desert.

considerations.text: Because of the traditional architecture, windows are on the small side, but most rooms and all suites have a balcony or terrace.
Dubai's city limits have expanded and the resort no longer feels quite so remote.
WhataHotel notes the desert location is away from the city's attractions.
